about: Facial expression model: FACS Action Units estimated from face-tracking signals, and expression prototypes defined over those AUs. Shared by the web (TypeScript) and iOS (Swift) engines. See docs/RESEARCH.md for the evidence behind every prototype and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for the scoring maths.

AU1.name: Inner brow raiser
AU1.look: Inner ends of the brows pulled up; brows become oblique; wrinkles in the centre of the forehead.

AU2.name: Outer brow raiser
AU2.look: Outer part of the brows lifted into an arch; wrinkles over the outer forehead.

AU4.name: Brow lowerer
AU4.look: Brows lowered and pulled together; vertical furrows between the brows.

AU5.name: Upper lid raiser
AU5.look: Eye opening widened; white of the eye shows above the iris.

AU6.name: Cheek raiser
AU6.look: Cheeks lifted, skin gathered around the eye, crow's-feet and a bulge under the lower lid. The 'Duchenne' marker.

AU7.name: Lid tightener
AU7.look: Lower lid tightened and raised; the eye narrows (squint).

AU9.name: Nose wrinkler
AU9.look: Skin along the nose wrinkles, nostril wings lift, inner brows are dragged down.

AU10.name: Upper lip raiser
AU10.look: Upper lip raised, nasolabial furrow deepened; upper lip may form an inverted U.

AU12.name: Lip corner puller
AU12.look: Lip corners pulled up and back (smile).

AU14.name: Dimpler
AU14.look: Lip corners tightened and drawn in, forming dimples. One-sided: the contempt sneer.

AU16.name: Lower lip depressor
AU16.look: Lower lip pulled down, exposing the lower teeth.

AU17.name: Chin raiser
AU17.look: Chin boss pushed up, lower lip pushed up and out; chin skin wrinkles (pout).

AU18.name: Lip pucker
AU18.look: Lips pulled forward into a pucker.

AU20.name: Lip stretcher
AU20.look: Lips stretched horizontally and flattened, corners pulled sideways (fear).

AU23.name: Lip tightener
AU23.look: Lips tightened; the red of the lips narrows.

AU25.name: Lips part
AU25.muscles: Depressor labii inferioris, or relaxation of mentalis / orbicularis oris

AU26.name: Jaw drop
AU26.muscles: Relaxation of masseter, temporalis, internal pterygoid

AU27.name: Mouth stretch
AU27.look: Mouth stretched wide open by actively pulling the jaw down.

AU28.name: Lip suck
AU28.look: Lips sucked in over the teeth.

AU41.name: Lid droop
AU41.look: Upper lids droop; eyes partly closed.

AU43.name: Eyes closed
AU43.muscles: Relaxation of levator palpebrae superioris; orbicularis oculi, pars palpebralis

AU51.name: Head turn left
AU51.look: Head turned to the person's left.

AU52.name: Head turn right
AU52.look: Head turned to the person's right.

AU55.name: Head tilt left
AU55.look: Head tilted towards the left shoulder.

AU56.name: Head tilt right
AU56.look: Head tilted towards the right shoulder.

GAZE_DOWN.name: Gaze averted down
GAZE_DOWN.muscles: Eyes and head together, relative to the camera
GAZE_DOWN.look: Looking down, away from the camera/viewer (head and eyes combined).

GAZE_AWAY.name: Gaze averted sideways
GAZE_AWAY.muscles: Eyes and head together, relative to the camera
GAZE_AWAY.look: Looking to the side, away from the camera/viewer (head and eyes combined).

PERCLOS.name: Eyelid closure over time (PERCLOS)
PERCLOS.look: Share of the last minute with the eyes at least 80% closed.

YAWN.name: Yawn
YAWN.look: Mouth held wide open for over a second.

STILL.name: Head stillness
STILL.look: How still the head has been over the last half second.

mediapipe.about: MediaPipe Face Landmarker (478 landmarks + 52 blendshapes) on an ordinary RGB camera. cheekSquint* and noseSneer* are never activated by MediaPipe's blendshape model, and eyeWide*/mouthFrown* are weak, so AU5, AU6, AU9, AU15 lean on landmark geometry (geo.*). Rest values and ranges were measured on 2,110 labelled faces; see docs/VALIDATION.md.

arkit.about: ARKit face tracking on the TrueDepth camera (iPhone X and later, including iPhone 16 Pro). All 52 blendshapes are active and depth-backed, so every AU maps directly. Rest values are conservative defaults; the per-user neutral calibration and adaptive baseline refine them.

expressions.name: Happiness
expressions.cues: Lip corners pulled up and back; cheeks raised with crow's-feet and a bulge under the lower lids in felt smiles; lips may part to show teeth.

expressions.name: Sadness
expressions.cues: Inner corners of the brows raised and drawn together (oblique 'grief' brows); lip corners pulled down; chin pushed up; lids droop and gaze falls. When crying: brows knitted, eyes squeezed, nose wrinkled, chin raised, lips stretched.

expressions.name: Surprise
expressions.gloss: Something unexpected — brief, neither positive nor negative by itself.
expressions.cues: Whole brow raised and curved, long horizontal forehead wrinkles; upper lids raised showing white above the iris; jaw dropped with relaxed, parted lips.

expressions.name: Fear
expressions.cues: Brows raised and pulled together (wrinkles only in the centre of the forehead); upper lids raised and lower lids tensed; lips stretched back horizontally, mouth often open.

expressions.name: Anger
expressions.cues: Brows lowered and drawn together with vertical furrows; hard stare — upper lids raised and/or lower lids tensed; lips pressed tight, or opened in a squarish shout (upper lip up, lower lip down).

expressions.name: Disgust
expressions.gloss: Revulsion at something offensive — tastes, smells, or moral violations.
expressions.cues: Nose wrinkled and upper lip raised; cheeks pushed up, lower lids raised; brows lowered; lower lip raised or pushed down and forward.

expressions.name: Contempt
expressions.gloss: Feeling superior to, or morally above, someone.
expressions.cues: One lip corner tightened and slightly raised (a one-sided dimple / sneer); often with the head tilted back, looking down the nose.

expressions.name: Happily surprised
expressions.gloss: Delight — pleasant surprise, good unexpected news.
expressions.cues: Surprise brows and dropped jaw combined with a smile.

expressions.name: Happily disgusted
expressions.cues: A smile together with a raised upper lip and wrinkled nose or lowered brows.

expressions.name: Sadly fearful
expressions.cues: Fear brows (raised and drawn together) and stretched lips, with sad lip corners rather than wide eyes.

expressions.name: Sadly angry
expressions.cues: Lowered, knitted brows and narrowed eyes with down-turned lip corners or a raised chin.

expressions.name: Sadly surprised
expressions.cues: Inner brows raised and pulled together with a dropped jaw.

expressions.name: Sadly disgusted
expressions.cues: Lowered brows and raised upper lip, with sad inner brows or down-turned lip corners.

expressions.name: Fearfully angry
expressions.cues: Lowered brows with stretched lips and a parted mouth.

expressions.name: Fearfully surprised
expressions.cues: Raised brows, very wide eyes, lips stretched and parted.

expressions.name: Fearfully disgusted
expressions.cues: Fear brows and stretched lips together with a raised upper lip.

expressions.name: Angrily surprised
expressions.cues: Lowered brows with a dropped jaw.

expressions.name: Angrily disgusted
expressions.cues: Lowered brows, raised upper lip and a raised chin.

expressions.name: Disgustedly surprised
expressions.cues: Surprise brows and wide eyes combined with a raised upper lip.

expressions.name: Appalled
expressions.gloss: Anger and disgust, with the weight on disgust.
expressions.cues: Lowered brows with a raised upper lip; cheeks raised, nose wrinkled.

expressions.name: Hatred
expressions.gloss: Anger and disgust, with the weight on anger.
expressions.cues: Lowered brows with a raised upper lip; lids tightened into a glare, lips pressed.

expressions.name: Awe
expressions.gloss: Wonder at something vast — fear and surprise, with the weight on surprise.
expressions.cues: Raised inner and outer brows, widened eyes and parted lips, often with the head tilted up.

expressions.name: Felt (Duchenne) smile
expressions.gloss: A smile that also engages the muscles around the eyes — classically read as felt enjoyment.
expressions.cues: Lip corners up (AU12) plus cheeks raised and crow's-feet (AU6). Note: AU6 also grows with smile intensity, so this is a cue, not proof.

expressions.name: Polite smile
expressions.gloss: A social or polite smile without eye involvement.
expressions.cues: Lip corners up without cheek raising or crow's-feet.

expressions.name: Amusement
expressions.cues: Broad smile with raised cheeks and an open mouth; head often thrown back, eyes may squeeze shut.

expressions.name: Embarrassment
expressions.cues: A controlled smile (lips pressed to suppress it), gaze averted down or aside, head turned away or down.

expressions.name: Shame
expressions.gloss: Feeling that one's self is flawed or exposed.
expressions.cues: Head bowed and gaze lowered, without a smile.

expressions.name: Pride
expressions.cues: A small smile with the head tilted back about 20°; in the body, an expanded posture.

expressions.name: Concentration
expressions.cues: Brows lowered and knitted, eyes narrowed, lips often pressed; no smile, mouth closed.

expressions.name: Confusion
expressions.cues: Brows lowered and knitted (AU4) with narrowed eyes (AU7), often with a head tilt, one brow raised or a sideways twist of the mouth.

expressions.name: Skepticism
expressions.cues: One eyebrow raised (a unilateral brow action), often with a lopsided mouth.

expressions.name: Interest
expressions.cues: Eyelids slightly widened, brows slightly raised, lips parted, head still with few glances away.

expressions.name: Worry
expressions.cues: Inner brows raised and drawn together (oblique brows) without a sad mouth; lips often pressed.

expressions.name: Boredom
expressions.cues: Drooping lids, head lowered or tilted, gaze wandering; yawning; little else moving.

expressions.name: Pain
expressions.cues: Brow lowering, orbital tightening (cheeks raised / lids tightened), levator contraction (nose wrinkle / upper lip raise), eyes squeezed shut — the PSPI actions.

expressions.name: Drowsiness
expressions.cues: Slow, long eyelid closures (high PERCLOS), drooping lids, yawning, nodding head.

expressions.name: Yawning
expressions.cues: Mouth stretched wide open for more than a second, eyes squeezed or closed.
